Hi Priyom,

Thanks for taking a look at our RFP. A few of our stakeholders reviewed Redwood's initial response and we need clarification on three items before procurement can move this to legal:

1) Platform fee amortization: the RFP asks for both annual and amortized pricing. Can you show an example of how Redwood proposesa platform fee when Evergreen wants a 3-year SOW but prefers to capitalize vs expense on the balance sheet?

2) Support tiers / on-call: we need a clear mapping of Bronze/Silver/Gold (hours, SLA, response times) and what is included vs what would be billed as an engineering retainer.

3) Deployment packaging: we want a single-bid option for an on-prem (air-gapped) Starter bundle and an option for a 2nd-phase production bundle that includes dedicated capacity. We also need to understand what discounts are available for upfront commit vs consumption-based billing.

Attached is the RFP (Evergreen_RFP_20261002.pdf). Our target go-live window is Q1 2027; procurement would like to start contracting this month. Can you get back with concrete examples and a proposed procurement timeline?

Thanks,

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and then we'll follow with a formal term sheet and SOW.

1) Platform fee amortization: Redwood can present both (a) an annualized platform fee that is invoiced yearly and (b) a capitalized/amortized approach where we present the platform fee as a single up-front invoice that Evergreen can amortize on your books. In practice: for a $900k platform fee we can show 12/24/36 month amortization examples; I'll attach a term-sheet snippet showing unit economics per month.

2) Support tiers: Bronze = business-hours support, 24-hour ticket SLA for P1, no on-call; Silver = business-hours + priority triage, 4-hour P1 initial response, 10 included engineering-hours/month for runbook/ops; Gold = 24x7 with 1-hour P1 response, 40 engineering-hours/month and quarterly on-site (or remote) runbooks. Additional engineering retainer hours priced separately or discounted when pre-purchased.

3) Packaging & discounts: Starter on-prem bundle (air-gapped) can be offered as a node-based SKU + platform fee (smaller footprint) with a low-commit discount (10% off platform fee for 12-month prepay). Production bundle (dedicated capacity + full telemetry) has higher platform fee but can be discounted 15–25% depending on commit and length. We can offer migration credits against the platform fee if you sign a 24+ month committed plan.

I've attached a short term-sheet (term-sheet-privdeploy-20261009.pdf) and a working SOW draft (SOW-draft-v2.docx) for internal review. Would you be available for a 30-minute call Tue 10/12 or Wed 10/13 to walk procurement and legal through the options?

Regards,

Priyom — thanks for the context. Below is a concise commercial proposal we can send as 'Option A / Option B' to Evergreen. Numbers here are examples (finalize once legal confirms phrasing).

Option A — Starter (recommended for Q1 pilot)
- Platform fee: $150,000 one-time (amortization examples: $150k/12=$12.5k/mo | /24=$6.25k/mo | /36=$4.17k/mo)
- Nodes: 3 on-prem nodes (air-gapped) + limited telemetry export; 6 cores equivalent/node baseline
- Support: Silver (4-hour P1 initial response, 10 eng-hrs/month included)
- Discount: 10% off platform fee for 12-month prepay; 15% off for 24-month prepay
- Migration credit: $15k credit applied to platform fee if commit >=24 months

Option B — Production (desired by Q1-Q2)
- Platform fee: $450,000 one-time (amortization examples: $450k/12=$37.5k/mo | /24=$18.75k/mo | /36=$12.5k/mo)
- Dedicated capacity: baseline throughput SLA, KV-cache priming, priority routing
- Support: Gold (1-hour P1 response, 40 eng-hrs/month, 2 quarterly runbook reviews)
- Discount: 15% off platform fee for 12-month commit with usage floors; 22% off for 24-month firm commit; up to 30% for 36-month strategic commit with case-by-case exec approval
- Engineering retainer: if pre-purchased in 6/12 month blocks, apply 20% credit against hourly rates (min 100 hours)

Additional notes:
- If Evergreen wants to present the platform fee as capital expenditure, we can issue a single invoice and provide amortization guidance for 12/24/36 months. That preserves Redwood cash collection (preferred) but we can also split into quarterly invoices if required.
- Attach the SOW-draft-v2.docx with a clear service description and acceptance criteria.
- Legal: recommend a CLM review for data residency wording in the SOW for air-gapped environments.

I'll prepare a one-page comparison and update the term-sheet to include the three amortization rows and the exact discounted line items.

Marissa
Director, Commercial Strategy
